newsitem.title: UK: FKI makes provision for reorganisation.
newsitem.headline: FKI makes provision for reorganisation.

text.p: British engineering group FKI Plc said on Friday it would make a provision of 21 million stg for its rationalisation of its electrical engineering division, including Hawker Siddeley Electric Power Group businesses and Marelli Motori.
The company said around 70 percent of the costs would be incurred in the year to March 1998 and the balance in the following year.

FKI said it was confident about its full year result despite the recent strength of sterling. It said the impact of exchange rates on overseas trading had been largely offset by a relatively strong U.S. market. Orders in its major export markets remained strong.
FKI said it remained confident last year's acquisition of Hawker Siddeley Electric Power Group and Marelli Motori would boost shareholder value by exceeding FKI's average cost of capital.
It said the Hawker Siddeley Electric Power Group had secured orders for 10 turbo generators from U.S. group Stewart & Stevenson.
Westinghouse Electric had ordered five large generators and there were orders for power and propulsion equipment for two seismic survey vessels to be built by Norway's Langsten Shipyards, FKI said.
FKI said the costs of its unsuccessful bid for Newman Tonks Plc totalled 3.5 million stg. That would be included in its results for the year to March 1997 as an exceptional item.
